transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-24
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Evan Morales (Orchid Head of Procurement), Priya Desai (Orchid Security Eng), Lena Park (Cloud Architect)

Summary (auto): Quick procurement + security preflight to align on MSA/DPA expectations, privileged keying (KMS/HSM) options, SSO/SAML integration, and an initial timeline for pilot & pricing approval. Agreed to exchange SOC2, security pack, and schedule an engineering pilot next week.

Topics: onboarding routing matrix, dedicated vs hosted egress, KMS integration, RBAC and tenant isolation, data residency, DPA redline items, pilot timeline and pricing pathing.

Action items (from call): Jordan to send security pack and SOC2; Maya to prepare perf costs; Priya to collate DPA requirements; schedule pilot.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Alright thanks everyone for joining, um today we wanted to walk through the sourcing matrix and the privileged keying questions you raised in the intake form. Hi Evan, Priya, Lena, thanks for making time.
[00:12] Evan Morales: Yeah, thanks Jordan. Sorry, short notice for some folks but we made it work, appreciate it. The key things for procurement are timeline and whether KMS or HSM options change the commercial path.
[00:25] Priya Desai: And from security we need clarity on where keys live, the key rotation model, and log/audit access. We also have minimums around SOC 2 type II and want to make sure there are clean audit trails.
[00:38] Maya Patel: Great, I can walk through the technical options — Redwood supports hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. For privileged keying we have two patterns: customer-managed KMS (you bring the key via KMS/HSM integration) or Redwood-managed keys with envelope encryption.
[00:54] Lena Park: Quick question, when you say "customer-managed KMS" can that be in our cloud account, like our AWS KMS? Or do you require an HSM appliance?
[01:05] Maya Patel: Yes, you can bring your AWS KMS key — we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault for private deployments. For hosted customers we usually do a customer-managed key via a KMS bridge; for fully on-prem we can support HSM appliances. There's a small ops extension to enable the key wrapping; it doesn't change tenant isolation.
[01:20] Evan Morales: That sounds promising. From procurement perspective, does customer-managed KMS introduce new fees or changes to the SLA?
[01:28] Jordan Lee: Good question. Customer-managed KMS itself doesn't usually change the base usage pricing, but we do have a nominal privileged-data handling addendum for HSM-backed keys and specific on-prem support, which is usually a one-time integration fee or part of the Dedicated contract. We'll put the exact bucketed numbers in the next email.
[01:46] Priya Desai: For compliance we need to ensure that key rotation policies can be enforced from our side and that Redwood won't retain raw keys. Is there a KMS policy doc we can see?
[01:55] Maya Patel: We'll share the KMS integration guide; in the customer-managed flow Redwood never sees plaintext keys — we only receive wrapped keys. There's also an option where we rotate a wrapping key, but you control the master key.
[02:08] Evan Morales: Okay, logging — if there is a request that triggers the KMS, will we get the audit events in our cloud logs or an aggregated Redwood audit log?
[02:15] Maya Patel: We can push audit events to your cloud monitoring (CloudWatch / Stackdriver / Monitor) for private and dedicated deployments. For hosted API we ship detailed audit logs to your SIEM via our log forwarding integration or SFTP. We'll include sample log formats in the security pack.
[02:30] Lena Park: Is there support for rotation windows and forced re-encrypts? Our data classification requires re-encryption within 72 hours of key rotation for some classes.
[02:40] Maya Patel: Re-encrypt patterns depend on whether the KV cache and prefix caching are in use; but yes, the platform can trigger rewrap/re-encrypt workflows. For strict timelines we recommend Dedicated or Private so we can schedule the rewrap jobs deterministically.
[02:56] Evan Morales: Got it. On the contracting side, our legal team will want the MSA redlined for two items — data residency guarantees and a clause about fallback routing if Redwood has an outage.
[03:07] Jordan Lee: Understood. We can propose an SLA addendum for routing fallback — e.g., automatic failover to a warmed reserve model variant in a different region. For data residency we have region pinning in Dedicated and Private, and we can map contractual residency commitments into the DPA.
[03:22] Priya Desai: Does Redwood provide a detailed data flow diagram for DPA attachments? We need a network and flow diagram for our auditors.
[03:28] Jordan Lee: Yes — I'll attach a system architecture diagram in the pack. It includes ingress/egress, KV cache boundaries, where the KMS calls happen, and retention defaults.
[03:37] Evan Morales: Perfect. One of the procurement constraints is timing — we have a board meeting on 2025-10-10 and we want a pricing commitment and legal redlines before that. Is that feasible?
[03:47] Jordan Lee: That's doable. If we have the DPA redlines by 2025-10-01 and confirm the deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private) we can route the deal to pricing and legal for a formal quote within a week. So yes, target 2025-10-07 for formal quote, 2025-10-10 for board.
[04:03] Lena Park: On performance, Maya, we mentioned latency targets in the intake — 95th percentile under 200ms for short prompts under our nominal batch size. Any flags?
[04:11] Maya Patel: That target is reasonable on Dedicated capacity for the model family you selected. Hosted can meet it for small volumes but if you need consistent SLAs we'd recommend Dedicated. We'll run a quick benchmark during the pilot; the initial perf sheet will show expected p95 given concurrency and batching settings.
[04:27] Priya Desai: About RBAC and tenant isolation — we need role separation: ops vs data stewards vs audit access. Is granular RBAC available out of the box?
[04:35] Maya Patel: Yes, the Console supports RBAC at the route/token level, plus audit trails. For Private we can add SAML groups mapping to roles. For Hosted we support SCIM provisioning to sync groups.
[04:44] Evan Morales: Does SCIM work with Okta?
[04:47] Jordan Lee: Yes, Okta and Azure AD are the most common. We'll include a quickstart for SSO and SCIM in the pack.
[04:55] Priya Desai: A slight concern — if we use customer-managed keys and a region pin, what happens to backups and logs? Residency applies to backups too, right?
[05:03] Maya Patel: Correct, backups for that tenant are stored in the selected region for Dedicated/Private. For hosted we can apply data residency constraints and egress routing to keep backups in-region — we'll document the guarantees and tie them to the DPA.
[05:16] Evan Morales: Okay, sounds like the big-ticket items are clear. On pricing: we likely need a transit fee estimate for egress if we go with cross-region failover and an ops onboarding fee for KMS/HSM support.
[05:28] Jordan Lee: We'll produce a pricing breakdown with line items for egress, reserved capacity, and privileged-keying onboarding. As mentioned earlier, customer-managed KMS doesn't typically change per-token pricing, but HSM or on-prem work does carry professional services fees.
[05:42] Lena Park: For the pilot, can we scope a short POC with around 50k tokens/day and a small model variant to validate latency and integration?
[05:49] Maya Patel: Absolutely. That's a perfect pilot size. We'll set up a dedicated reserved pool for the pilot or use a private VPC evaluation instance — whichever fits your network posture.
[05:59] Evan Morales: One more procurement nuance — our finance team needs to know whether the deal can be net-60 or net-30. Do you have flexibility?
[06:06] Jordan Lee: For small pilots we can do net-60 with a credit card or escrow for larger deals we typically default to net-30 but we can route to finance for exceptions. We'll flag finance flexibility in the quote.
[06:18] Priya Desai: Any competitor-specific tradeoffs we should note? We did a bake off with Anthropic and OpenAI; our security team likes Anthropic's hosted key options but pricing was a blocker. We want to make sure we can show clear security alignment.
[06:31] Jordan Lee: We can call out where Redwood's private and customer-managed KMS flows match or differ from the competitors in the security pack. We'll highlight the audit capabilities and enterprise RBAC.
[06:42] Lena Park: Operationally, how does token-level cost attribution work? Our product team needs per-feature cost reporting.
[06:49] Maya Patel: The Console exposes per-route and per-token cost breakdowns, and we can export token-level usage for billing reconciliation. We'll show you sample exports in CSV.
[06:58] Evan Morales: Alright, great. Let's go to the recap and next steps.
[07:03] Jordan Lee: Recap: Jordan will send the security pack, SOC2, and the system diagram by 2025-09-30. Maya will prepare a performance/egress spreadsheet and pilot config by 2025-10-03. Priya will send DPA redline priorities and KMS requirements by 2025-10-02. We aim to have a formal quote by 2025-10-07 to present at your 2025-10-10 board meeting.
[07:24] Evan Morales: That covers it. I'll loop in legal and finance after those artifacts arrive. Thanks Jordan and Maya.
[07:31] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the pilot kickoff.
[07:36] (call ends)

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-heard product names ("Redwind" or "Redwood Dedicated" heard as "Redwind Dedicated") and minor speaker label jitter; confirmed medium transcription quality.
